Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
Inversion after a negative adverb carries stress on the auxiliary: Rarely HAS the board; Not until June DID the ministry. The fronted phrase itself is usually unstressed.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Fronting for Focus.

Front an element when the rest of the sentence depends on it. Keep the neutral order when nothing is at stake, because heavy fronting reads as rhetoric. With negative or limiting fronting, invert: Rarely has the board, Not until June did the ministry, Under no circumstances will we.

fronted adverbial — sets time, place or condition: In the third quarter, the deficit doubled
negative fronting — inverts subject and operator: Rarely has the board seen such a vote
not until / only when — inverts, often with a delay: Only when the audit ended did the scale emerge
fronted object — topicalises the object: That the plan was rushed, the auditors never denied
fronted complement — inversion with be: Such was the outcry that the plan was withdrawn
fronted particle — inversion in narrative: Out of the negotiation walked the smaller delegation
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence inverts correctly?
options: Never have I seen such a result.
Never have seen I such a result.
Never I have seen such a result.

elements.content: 2. Which fronted element triggers inversion?
3. Complete: 'Such ___ the demand that tickets sold out.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

Time — In the third quarter of last year, the deficit doubled. (A fronted adverbial sets the frame.)
Negative — Rarely has the board seen such a divided vote. (A negative front triggers inversion.)
Object — That the plan was rushed, the auditors never denied. (A fronted object is topicalised, not inverted.)
Particle — Out of the negotiation walked the smaller delegation. (Inversion after a particle.)
What do you observe?

Fronting moves an element out of its neutral position to the start of the clause, which makes it the frame for everything that follows. When the fronted element is negative or limiting (never, rarely, not until, under no circumstances), the subject and operator invert. When it is a plain adverbial or object, the order of subject and verb does not change.
1. Does 'In June the report appeared' need inversion?
options: No: the fronted element is a plain adverbial.
Yes, always after a fronted phrase.

elements.content: 2. Why front a phrase?
options: To make it the frame the reader holds while reading the rest.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.

Success criteria:
- I can front an adverbial to set the frame of a sentence.
- I can invert after never, rarely, not until and under no circumstances.
- I can keep the neutral order when fronting would add nothing.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ Rarely the board has seen such a vote (no inversion after a negative adverb) → ✅ Rarely has the board seen such a vote
❌ In the third quarter, doubled the deficit (verb before subject after a plain adverbial) → ✅ In the third quarter, the deficit doubled
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

Should the offer be withdrawn, we will renegotiate.
Only after the vote did the scale of the split appear.
This point the minister did not address.
